label: Uneasy
summary: The Gulf is still the heaviest weight. Houthi forces struck Aramco facilities hours after a Saudi-led coalition hit an oil site in Sanaa, and the WHO reported cholera cases surging in Yemen. A Russian missile hit a Kyiv power plant, further dimming hopes for an energy ceasefire. Deaths from storms in Mexico rose to five. Markets steadied after Tuesday's Asian sell-off: Singapore's economy grew more than 5% on AI demand, though Brent crude stayed near $106. There were small openings for diplomacy. A UN official saw a window for peace in DR Congo, and Colombia's peace tribunal charged former FARC members over crimes against Indigenous people. Science supplied the brightest news, including the first drug in 30 years for a deadly brain disease, and an Italian biomethane plant came online. The weighted formula gave 41; no editorial adjustment.
